content.comment_body: Hello, From what I know, there is a maximum of 400 function blocks in a [product_name] program. Is there any method to increase this limit, such as inserting an MMC, or is it fixed? Thanks.
You can connect to a second [product_name] for expansion.

Here's a tip: Since 400 function blocks is the maximum, you can save blocks by using the input inversion feature on function blocks. When you insert a FB, the left side shows its inputs. If you move your cursor to an FB input and right-click, you can invert the signal. Many [product_name] programmers aren't aware of this and use an additional NOT-FB for inversion. Instead, try inverting the inputs directly, which doesn't count as extra function blocks. See the attached image for reference. Hope this helps.
Here's another easy way to save a block. See image.
Actually, that's incorrect. The high and low blocks are constants, not function blocks.
If you still experience the problem (even without using the invert block), consider switching to another PLC series, such as [version_no] or another model.
What you posted does not relate to the main topic.

Is it possible to have more than one master [product_name] in a configuration? The master [product_name] runs the user program. You can add slave [product_name] modules for additional IO, but these do not execute the user program.

Yes, you can have more than one master unit. When referring to "slave," it only pertains to the communication relationship between the [product_name] devices, not their programming roles. This means you can distribute control, with each unit managing its own area and exchanging relevant data. The master/slave terminology is about communication, not control; multiple masters are possible but not required. Was this useful?
Hello [user_name], I don't think [user_name] had a question; it seems more like a comment or observation.
Hi, good to hear from you. You’re probably right – I missed that [user_name] was responding to their own post. Even so, I think my reply still adds to the discussion.

Thanks for the clarification. I'm running out of function blocks in the master [product_name], so I need to split the user program over several devices. That's the idea behind this topic. I have a few questions: 1) Can a slave [product_name] module execute a program, and where is the diagram entry created for it? 2) Looking at connection properties, the link between master1 and HMI or another master uses TSAP. For a master-slave link, TSAP is not used. What's the difference? 3) On Master1 at 192.168.0.150, what is the port seen at the bottom left of this device? My setup: 192.168.0.150 is the master, and in the project overview the diagram is generated automatically for Master1. 192.168.0.151 is the slave; no diagram file is created for it. How do you add a diagram for this module? 192.168.0.152 is a second master, and here a diagram is automatically created.

1) A slave [product_name] can execute a program, but no diagram is created for it. 2) As a slave, it doesn’t communicate independently; only the master initiates communication, so TSAPs aren't relevant. 3) I have no information about the 'double box'.

I believe I now understand the function of the 'double box' symbol in network mode. The device can create up to 8 static and 16 dynamic TCP/IP connections. Static connections require TSAPs on the server side, while dynamic ones only need TSAPs on the client. I tested a project with 11 units, 8 with static connections and 3 with dynamic. Please refer to the attached manual extract.
Thank you for clarifying the network features of [product_name] 8. Using multiple masters helps overcome the 400 function block limitation I encountered in my project. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is constrained by a strict limit of 400 function blocks in a [product_name] 8 program. Solutions discussed include utilizing additional networked modules to partition the logic, and optimizing programming methods to use fewer blocks. There is some confusion over what types of elements count toward the limit, particularly regarding constant blocks and NOT functions, which affects understanding and usability.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for a way to increase the function block limit for [product_name] 8 programs, whether by hardware upgrades or software workarounds. They are also seeking clarification on whether the limitation can be bypassed and want efficiency tips if it cannot.
